393.author: nicolas carrara
393.diff:
@@ -9,9 +9,9 @@ rule_references: []
 
~
 ## Question
~
 
~
 Q: The 1.5 errata states that "Any model that is within a fighting rank
-and within a number of inches equal to its
  Movement of the enemy unit can fight." The Random Movement special rule states that "Models with this special rule do not have a normal Movement characteristic. Instead, a dice roll is given (2D6, for example). When a model with this special rule moves, roll the dice to determine its maximum movement." How should this interaction be played?
~
 
~
 ## Ruling
~
 
~
 A) Because the unit does not have a normal movement characteristic when not actively moving, treat the movement value during combat as M (-). This means that models with Random Movement can only make attacks when in base contact with an enemy model. 
+Hello world!?
~
 B) Those units still have a Movement characteristic that deviates from the norm. When a unit with Random Movement has models in a fighting rank but not in base-to-base contact with an enemy models, roll their Random Movement dice when their combat is chosen during step 1.1 of the Combat phase. Use the number rolled as the unit's Movement for this combat phase as the unit's Movement characteristic when determining which models outside of base-to-base can attack. If the 
+OK
  unit with Random Movement fights in a 2nd combat during the same combat phase, when that new combat is chosen the unit with Random Movement will roll again to determine this range.
~

entry.question: Q: The GW FAQ says that an effect which can re-roll a failed casting roll does not work on a miscast. Does this ruling also apply to effects that allow you to re-roll any casting roll, such as Tome of Spellcraft?
entry.ruling: Yes, the ruling states that a miscast cannot be re-rolled and this applies regardless of the type of re-roll ability.
entry.rule_references:
GW FAQ
Tome of Spellcraft
Buzgob's Knobbly Staff

412.author: nicolas carrara
412.diff:
@@ -10,9 +10,11 @@ rule_references:
 
~
 ## Question
~
 
~
 The rule for 
-Transformation of the Dragon states that the new form cannot be placed within 1" of friendly models, within 3" and within 6" of its previous form. The new FAQ states that when the Dragon is in
+Tin
  base-to-base contact with enemy models and transforms, it must remain in b2b. As it's impossible to satisfy all of these conditions, how should the rule be played? What happens if there is no room for the new model to be in b2b with the enemy unit?
~
 
~
 ## Ruling
~
 
~
 When a Cathayan Dragon is in combat, their transformation rule ignores the requirements to be further than 1" from friendly models or 3" from enemy models and their base is allowed to overlap their previous form.
~
 If there is no room to place the new model in b2b with the enemy unit due to allied models occupying their full front arc, simply nudge those friendly units aside by the minimum distance necessary to fit the Dragon's new form. However, if there is no space to fit the new Dragon model due to enemy units (even ignoring the 1" rule) or allied units not engaged in the combat, the dragon cannot transform.
~
~
+hello world
~

entry.question: Some special rules use the wording majority of the models (Warband, Immune to Psychology, Frenzy, Run with the Pack as examples). How do these special rules work when there is no majority, and the unit is split half?
entry.ruling: Unlike Motley Crew, all these rules are optional or buffs to existing rules. For Motley Crew, the rules stop working on a draw, but these rules are full functional. Thus, you need to have more than 50% of the models qualifying for the use of the rule to achieve a majority and make the rule work.

67.diff:
@@ -20,15 +20,14 @@ What about evasive or lone character protection against such abilities?
 Besides the attacks with Missile weapons units do when selected in the shooting phase for shooting, the following abilities are considered to be shooting or shooting attacks:
~
 - Abilities that inflict hits, wounds suffered or wounds lost against a target are shooting attacks
~
 - Magic Missiles and Vortexes are defined as shooting, if they have a target or not
~
 - Any ability that is introduced as 
-"shooting
+"shootizrzarzrng
  " or "instead of shooting normally" or an "attack in the shooting phase" or being "used in the shooting phase" (Column of Fire, Pidgeon Bomb, Wailing Dirge, Breath Weapon  etc.) is shooting
~
 
~
 Anything else happening in the Shooting Phase is not a shooting attack (Zzzap! Ability of the Doomwheel)
~
 
~
 You cannot use a Shooting Attack or Shooting after you marched (including abilities that can be used in combat like Wailing Dirge or Storm Call)
~
 
~
 Evasive and Lone Character Protection can be used against:
~
 - Any of those abilities affirmed to be shooting/attacks above 
-that have a single target unit/model (and normal shooting)
~
-- Breath Weapons and any of those abilities with intended target, if the unit to be protected or using evasive is the intended target. The intended target is the unit you aim to hit the most models possible of. This means you cannot try to hit a character if that means you hit less models of the intended target unit.
~
-- Cannon Fire and Column of Fire can only have evasive used against them if the target point/template lies on
+thon
  a models base.
~
 
~
 Evasive and Lone Character Protection cannot be used against any of those abilites that have no target (Burning Gaze, Gaze of Gork, Strangleroots, Cannon Fire if the target point was not on the models base).
~
+sqdfsqdfsdf
~

entry.question: Some abilities grant bonuses to a characteristic, up to a maximum value. Some grant bonuses with no mention of a maximum value. When used together, how do they interact? How does it interact with Strike Last, Strike First or abilities that set characteristics to a certain value?
entry.ruling: Set the Initiative first to the value (1 in case of Strike Last). Any limitation is applied at the end of characteristic calculation. If there are no limitations on the characteristic from any source, you can go above 10. Note that no characteristic can go below 0 (see pg. 97 Characteristics of Zero). Models with Initiative 0 attack in Initiative order, after all attacks with initiative 1, including stomp attacks.
entry.rule_references:
Model Profiles CRB 96 - 97
Tomb Kings My Will Be done RH 126

entry.question: How do Items interact that let you throw an additional dice and discard the lowest and items that enforce you to roll an additional dice and discard the highest? Do they cancel themselves out so you just roll 2 dice or do they make you roll 4 dice discarding highest and lowest (making double 1s even more likely)
entry.ruling: You would roll 4 dice, discarding the highest and the lowest.
